terms.def: A unit of flow: one cubic foot per second, about 28.3 litres per second. A flow of 1,000 cusecs is about 28 cubic metres per second.
Thousand million cubic feet. One TMC is 1,000 mcft, about 28.3 million cubic metres of water.
Million cubic feet. One mcft is about 28,300 cubic metres of water.
Million litres per day, a common way to state city water supply and treatment capacity.
Full reservoir level: the highest level a reservoir is designed to hold in normal operation.
Empty space kept in a reservoir below its full level so it can absorb floodwater.
The strip of land at a lake's edge that is covered when the water level rises.
Comptroller and Auditor General of India, the national government audit body.
Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority, the city's planning body.
National Remote Sensing Centre, part of ISRO.
Synthetic aperture radar: satellite radar that images the ground through cloud and at night, useful for mapping floods.
A pair of European Space Agency radar satellites often used to map floods.
Seawater reverse osmosis: pushing seawater through membranes at high pressure to make fresh water.
The pressure needed to stop water crossing a membrane from the fresh side to the salty side. Reverse osmosis must exceed it.
The ratio of the minimum energy a process needs, set by thermodynamics, to the energy it actually uses.
Common effluent treatment plant: a shared plant that treats wastewater from many small factories.
Zero liquid discharge: treating industrial wastewater so no liquid leaves the site, leaving recovered water and solid waste.
A synthetic dye containing a nitrogen-to-nitrogen double bond. Azo dyes are widely used in textiles and resist breakdown.
An enzyme that oxidises many organic compounds, including some dyes.
Using fungi to break down or remove pollutants.
Passing genes between organisms other than from parent to offspring, which lets resistance genes spread between bacterial species.
A small circular piece of DNA that bacteria can copy and pass to one another.
Single-nucleotide polymorphism: a one-letter difference in DNA. The SNP distance between two isolates counts how many such differences separate them.
Dynamic difficulty adjustment: changing a game's difficulty while it is being played.
Engagement optimized matchmaking: pairing players to keep them playing longer, not to make matches fair.
Squad Building Challenge: an Ultimate Team task that rewards a pack in exchange for handing in a set of players.
A game built to be updated and monetised continuously after launch instead of sold as a finished product.
In Hindu cosmology, the fourth and present age of the world. Traditional reckoning dates its start to 3102 BCE.
Steel made by melting iron and carbon together in a sealed clay pot, which gives a uniform high-carbon metal.
Crucible steel made in southern India from at least the third century BCE, later known in Europe as Damascus steel.
A maritime empire centred on Sumatra that controlled trade through the Strait of Malacca.
The impact crater beneath Mexico's Yucatan peninsula, linked to the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs.
